card.name: Conditional wording before a clause or comparison
card.fires_on: Words that open a condition or exception in dosing text, such as 'not' in 'reaction not listed', 'necessary', 'avoided', 'requiring', 'more' and 'other' before 'than'. Also the middle of words like 'concomitant' and 'dilations'.

modes.label: Condition or exception word
modes.description: A word like not, necessary, avoided or requiring that sets up an if-case or exception in a dosing instruction.
modes.example: If dose reduction is required due to an adverse reaction<< not>> listed in Table 2, then reduce

modes.label: Comparison word before than
modes.description: The word more or other right before 'than' and an amount.
modes.example: For patients who require concentrations<< other>> than 500 mcg/mL

modes.label: Partway through a word
modes.description: The middle or end of a word such as concomitant or dilations.
modes.example: proate. Serious skin reactions (such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis) have been reported with concom<<itant>> lamotrigine and valproate
